newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile tells Spain it won't recognize Pinochet trial.
newsitem.headline: Chile tells Spain it won't recognize Pinochet trial.

text.p: Chile has told Spain it will not recognise the authority of a Madrid court to try former military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet for the killings of Spanish citizens during his rule, officials said on Friday.

Chilean Justice Minister Soledad Alvear told officials in Madrid on Thursday that her government would not accept the jurisdiction of courts in other countries over crimes committed on Chilean soil, even if the crimes involved foreign citizens, the foreign ministry officials said.
"Chile will not recognise the authority of other countries to judge cases committed on our territory," one of the officials quoted Alvear as telling Spanish authorities.

The officials declined to say if Alvear's statements meant Chile would not cooperate at all with judge Manuel Garcia Castellon's investigations into human rights abuses committed against about 10 Spaniards during Pinochet's rule.

The Spaniards were among some 3,000 Chileans killed after being detained by security forces during Pinochet's rule from 1973 to 1990. Pinochet, 81, remains commander-in-chief of the army until next March.

Alvear was reported to have expressed Chile's "concern" about the trial and Chilian officials said President Eduardo Frei's government viewed the trial as a judgment not just of Pinochet, but of Chile's whole transition to democracy.
The Chilean government is eager to erase memories of Pinochet's harsh rule and the international opprobrium that accompanied it.
